sources.title: Non-surgical interventions for treating osteoarthritis of the big toe joint.
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2024-06-17. Version/access details below.

access.details: Cochrane summary and indexed PMC review discussion/characteristics inspected; Europe PMC XML returned 500. Entire review inspection not completed, conservatively classified abstract-only.

sources.design: 2024 Cochrane review, six trials and 547 participants; minor amendment noted January 2025.
sources.population: First-MTP/big-toe OA; a small functional hallux-limitus trial is indirect.
sources.comparator: Three placebo/sham comparisons; other trials used active treatment.
sources.coInterventions: Varied devices, injections and multimodal care.
sources.outcomes: Moderate-certainty evidence of no clinically important benefit from arch-contouring orthoses or shoe-stiffening inserts versus sham; other treatments/exercise remain uncertain.
sources.followUp: Longest 52 weeks; primary review endpoint 12 weeks.
sources.uncertainty: Few trials and limited exercise evidence; functional hallux-limitus findings may be indirect for radiographic OA. Partial full-review inspection conservatively classified abstract-only.
sources.harms: Serious events not reported; device events commonly foot pain.
sources.limitations: Few trials and limited exercise evidence; functional hallux-limitus findings may be indirect for radiographic OA. Partial full-review inspection conservatively classified abstract-only. Research candidate only; no clinical release.
locations: Authors conclusions; Discussion > Summary of main results (indexed sections)

sources.title: Effectiveness of Foot Orthoses Versus Rocker-Sole Footwear for First Metatarsophalangeal Joint Osteoarthritis: Randomized Trial.
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2016-05-01. Version/access details below.

access.details: Full indexed publisher methods/results inspected. Europe PMC core metadata identifies linked 2018 erratum 10.1002/acr.23732; its full content remains unavailable and is not presumed trivial. https://acrjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/acr.22750

integrity.method: Publisher/PubMed records inspected during research; Europe PMC REST core metadata DOI:10.1002/acr.22750 rechecked during serialization, including publication type and comment/correction links. Not a registry-wide clearance.
integrity.result: Linked notices: Erratum in: Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken). 2018 Sep;70(9):1420. doi: 10.1002/acr.23732 No claim of exhaustive integrity clearance or automatic supersession.

sources.design: Randomised active-device trial, n=102, with linked 2018 erratum.
sources.population: Symptomatic first-MTP OA; recurrent fallers excluded.
sources.comparator: Modified prefabricated orthoses versus rocker-sole shoes.
sources.outcomes: Originally reported FHSQ difference 2.05 (95% CI −3.61 to 7.71), with similar improvement. Shoes had lower adherence and more adverse events (39% versus 16%; RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.12–5.44). The linked erratum text is unavailable: check these numbers against the correction before release.
sources.uncertainty: Active comparison without sham cannot isolate efficacy. A linked 2018 erratum remains unread; original numerical values require correction review before release. Device exclusions do not establish exercise contraindications.
sources.harms: Original trial reported more shoe events, including new low-back pain; implications of the erratum remain unresolved.
sources.limitations: Active comparison without sham cannot isolate efficacy. A linked 2018 erratum remains unread; original numerical values require correction review before release. Device exclusions do not establish exercise contraindications. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Modified full-length prefabricated orthoses with first-metatarsal cut-out versus MBT rocker-sole shoes.
protocol.dose: Device use rather than exercise; exact wearing schedule beyond the 12-week assignment not re-extracted.
protocol.frequency: 12-week device use, with adherence measured in hours.
protocol.progression: not reported as exercise load progression.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as exercise stopping rules.

sources.uncertainty: No superiority of contoured orthoses over sham; not a test of motion restrictions or exercise. Entire primary article inspection not completed.
sources.harms: Generally minor/transient; exact event table not completely re-extracted.
sources.limitations: No superiority of contoured orthoses over sham; not a test of motion restrictions or exercise. Entire primary article inspection not completed. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

sources.design: Small controlled clinical trial, n=20, not an established-OA-specific RCT.
sources.population: Functional hallux limitus with pain, motion loss and weakness; not necessarily radiographic OA.
sources.comparator: Multimodal physiotherapy alone versus added mobilisation/strength/gait bundle.
sources.coInterventions: Both groups received whirlpool, ultrasound, toe mobilisation, calf/hamstring stretching, marble pickup, cold and electrical modalities.
sources.outcomes: The added bundle improved ROM, flexor strength and pain after 12 visits (P<.001); isolated exercise effect and durability remain unknown.
sources.uncertainty: Small functional hallux-limitus multimodal trial, indirect for radiographic OA. Full exact exercise methods and harms unavailable; no isolated strengthening effect.
sources.harms: not reported in the accessible abstract.
sources.limitations: Small functional hallux-limitus multimodal trial, indirect for radiographic OA. Full exact exercise methods and harms unavailable; no isolated strengthening effect. Research candidate only; no clinical release.
